result.title: Who Should Know What? Empirical Information Design for Multi-Agent LLM Economies
result.summary: The performance of multi-agent LLM systems depends not only on the capabilities of the underlying models but also on information-sharing policies, which govern what information each agent observes and at what level of detail. But does providing AI agents with more detailed information always improve collective outcomes, or can transparency paradoxically degrade efficiency? To investigate this, we introduce empirical information design, an experimental framework that systematically compares disclosure policies across economic markets populated by LLM agents, while holding interaction rules and models fixed. We evaluate ten frontier LLMs in multi-resource trade, bilateral bargaining, and double auctions, using ground-truth utilities to decouple identified opportunities from realized outcomes. We find that finer information disclosure yields highly model-dependent results. In trade, revealing exact valuations rather than ordinal preference rankings reduces realized gains for GPT-6 Sol (from 98% to 91% of maximum) yet increases them for Claude Sonnet 5 (from 72% to 86%). In bargaining, exact information leads Grok 4.7 to produce less balanced agreements, whereas Claude Opus 5.5 divides gains symmetrically. In double auctions, full disclosure inflates price demands, triggering market breakdown and lowering welfare for Gemini 3.1 Pro (97% to 78%), Claude Opus 5.5 (94% to 64%), and Grok 4.7 (97% to 62%). Overall, these results suggest that model selection and information design must be co-optimized, as LLMs vary in how their strategic responses to information impact system objectives.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「经验性信息设计」框架，在固定交互规则与模型的前提下，比较 LLM 代理在交易、双边议价和双向拍卖中接收不同粒度信息披露（如精确估值与序数偏好、完全披露与部分披露）时的集体结果，并对十个前沿模型做对照实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作考察披露信息粒度如何改变代理的决策与集体效率，可为 LVR 中「视觉证据该保留多少细节」「信息坍缩的代价是否随模型而异」的假设提供类比性核查线索，但其观察对象是外部披露策略而非内部 latent 状态，迁移需谨慎。
